objective.statement: Recognise staccato, legato and accent marks and say how to play them.
successCriteria: I know a dot over a note means staccato: short and detached.
I know a slur means legato: smooth and joined.
I know a > sign is an accent: emphasise the note.

explanation.text: Articulation tells the player how to attack and shape each note. It is shown with small marks above or below the notes.

music.textAlternative: Four crotchets each with a dot: staccato.

explanation.caption: Staccato: a dot over or under the note. Play it short and detached.

music.textAlternative: Four different notes under one long curved line: legato.

explanation.caption: Legato: a curved line over different notes. Play them smoothly, joined together.

music.textAlternative: A first note with an accent sign, followed by three plain notes.

explanation.caption: Accent: a > sign. Emphasise the note, play it with a stronger attack.

explanation.text: Staccato = short. Legato = smooth. Accent = stress.

music.textAlternative: Two staccato notes followed by two notes under a slur.

steps: Look at the first two notes: each has a dot. Imagine playing them short and separate.
The last two notes are under a curve: imagine them smoothly joined.
Notice the same rhythm can feel very different with different articulation.
demonstration.textAlternative: Two staccato notes followed by two legato notes under a slur.
